transcript: I did not expect to be emotionally destroyed by Old Friends on Broadway, but in retrospect, I really should have known better. This is a tribute to the legendary composer Stephen Sondheim and stars Bernadette Peters and Lea Salonga, along with a fantastic ensemble and orchestra. It's a two-act staged concert with about forty songs, and while the music speaks for itself, throwing in a Broadway budget never hurts. This is a very comprehensive journey through Sondheim’s catalogue, and I didn't read the song list beforehand which made for some really lovely surprises and emotional gut punches. It was also refreshing to experience an evening of musical theater where many different voice types were represented — not just everyone belting as high as they can, which is the case in a lot of contemporary scores. But what really got me was how overwhelming it was to bask in the scope of Sondheim’s catalogue. It brought my attention to just how prolific he was and how crazy it is for one person to have had such a profound impact on an entire art form. He was truly one of a kind, and it's hard to overstate the role that he has played in the soundtrack to so many people's lives, including mine. Old Friends is currently running at the Friedman on Broadway through June 15th. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer expresses strong emotional connection ('emotionally destroyed') and overwhelming appreciation for the comprehensive journey through Sondheim's work. While not explicitly stating 'go see this,' the passionate tone, multiple positive elements highlighted, and reverent discussion of Sondheim's impact clearly signal enthusiastic recommendation.
